site_name: Google Berkeley County Data Center (Mount Holly Commerce Park)
serving_utility: Berkeley Electric Cooperative (power supplied through Central Electric Power Cooperative from Santee Cooper)
load_basis: Santee Cooper's statement in a May 2025 contract dispute with the cooperatives that the long-running Google data center 'uses upwards of 380 megawatts'. This is a demand figure asserted by the wholesale supplier, not a metered annual average and not critical IT capacity.
notes: One campus. All of these known_facilities fids are the same campus and should collapse into this row: osm:way/626226408, osm:way/610827836, osm:way/1069388067, osm:way/1069388075, osm:way/1069388095, osm:way/1069388141, osm:way/1069388147, osm:way/1069388156, osm:way/1069388186, osm:way/1069388211, bi:867-0 (the 2022 date on bi:867-0 is a later building or generator permit, not first operation). Coordinates are the OSM campus outline already in the inventory; city from Google's 2021 expansion release (https://www.charlestondigital.com/news/1616089156391-google-announces-500-million-investment-berkeley-county-data-center-expansion). Year: Google's page says the data center 'was built in 2007' and the SC Daily Gazette says it has operated since 2007; some accounts date first operations to 2008, hence medium. Utility: NRECA's RE Magazine says Google set up along Berkeley Electric Cooperative's lines about 20 years ago; the 2025 dispute is over the Santee Cooper to Central contract terms for this one load, hence special_contract. The 380 MW figure was read from search-result excerpts of the Gazette article (the page itself returned 403 to a direct fetch), and it exceeds EPRI's 2024 statewide average of 203 MW by itself, so treat it as peak or contract demand. Expansion continues (Google announced further Berkeley County investment in 2024 and 2025); no full-buildout MW published.

site_name: NYDIG Spartanburg bitcoin mine (former Greenidge South Carolina facility, 300 Jones Road)
operator: NYDIG (built by Greenidge Generation; sold to NYDIG November 2023)
load_basis: Built mining capacity: Greenidge completed the expansion to 44 MW in August 2023 and its FY2024 10-K describes the sold site as '44 MW South Carolina mining facilities'. Whether NYDIG ran all 44 MW through 2025 is not confirmed.
notes: Address from the SC Department of Commerce release ('175 acres at 300 Jones Road in Spartanburg'), geocoded with the U.S. Census geocoder. Former LSC Communications printing plant. Greenidge's FY2021 10-K: 'We commenced small scale mining operations, using portable equipment, at the Spartanburg facility in December 2021.' Sale of the mining facility and about 22 acres to NYDIG closed 9 November 2023 (FY2024 10-K). Utility: WFAE says the Upstate site is served by Duke Energy; Greenidge's filings do not name the supplier, hence medium. Separate from this row: Greenidge's remaining 152 acres with rights to 60 MW of future service (expected September 2026) were under contract to a Lightstone Group subsidiary in December 2025 (https://theenergymag.com/news/2025-12-03/greenidge-south-caroline-sale-bitcoin); that is a future data center, not 2025 load. Greenidge's FY2021 10-K projected at least 100 MW of mining capacity for the whole original site, not adopted here as a buildout figure.

site_name: SWI Digital (formerly Genesis Digital Assets) Anderson bitcoin mine
operator: SWI Digital (formerly Genesis Digital Assets, GDA)
load_basis: Capacity announced by the operator at opening (18 MW, online February 2023). Operating status and load in 2025 not confirmed.
notes: Reused abandoned textile warehouse near Anderson; no street address published in any source read, so no coordinates. Utility is low confidence: the operator's own site lists one South Carolina data center, labeled 'Greenville', and says it uses energy from Duke Energy; it is an assumption that this page describes the Anderson facility. County per SC Biz News headline (Anderson and Union counties).

site_name: SWI Digital (formerly Genesis Digital Assets) Union-Lockhart bitcoin mines (two sites, combined)
operator: SWI Digital (formerly Genesis Digital Assets, GDA)
load_basis: Combined capacity of two facilities announced by the operator at opening (15 MW together, online March 2023); no per-site split published, so each site may be under 10 MW. Operating status and load in 2025 not confirmed.
notes: TWO separate facilities 'between the towns of Union and Lockhart' reported as one 15 MW figure; kept as one row because no split or addresses were published. One is described as near Pacolet and near two Lockhart Power hydro plants. GDA's release names Lockhart Power as the energy supplier for the site near its hydro plants; whether both sites are on Lockhart Power's retail system is not stated, hence medium. No coordinates.

site_name: Meta Aiken Data Center (Sage Mill Industrial Park)
serving_utility: Aiken Electric Cooperative (member of Central Electric Power Cooperative)
load_basis: Not operating in 2025: SC Daily Gazette (via Yahoo, 25 Aug 2025) describes the data center as under construction and 'expected to be completed in 2027'. Meta's fact sheet still speaks of the campus in the future tense.
notes: Included to correct the existing record, which carries a 2026 start and 129 MW counted as load today. Sources read show no building in operation in 2025 and completion expected in 2027; no first-operation date has been published, so energized_year is null. No street address found, so lat/lon left null; keep the existing record's coordinates. Meta's fact sheet says it 'worked with Aiken Electric Cooperative to plan for our energy needs' and pays the full cost of its energy, read here as a negotiated arrangement (special_contract). Meta has not published a load figure; the 129 MW in the inventory was not verified by any source read.
